# The owner's veto list

> **FINAL (draft 15). The state at the final tree** (the doors' seat's final tip: lane/tail-close-doors-2026-11-15 at d6884c590; 70 commits over the line, all signed Claude): every refreshed test file is green when run alone (38 files), the build checks are green (603 tests) and the fourteen steps of the check that are not tests exit 0. ONLY THE OWNER'S THREE DOOR FILES STAY RED BY NAME (the map calibration 30 of 32, the description manifest 14 of 17, the lighting sample 6 of 7): they wait on the owner's explicit word (see the Part E entry at the head of Part E and of the short list). The chair's own whole check of the landed line runs next and takes about 105 minutes; its result is told to the owner in the chat, not in this list. Nothing on this list has been merged or deployed by this seat.
> **About the short list:** the chair asked for at most 40 entries and for an own entry for every change touching 100 or more sample towns. These two cannot both hold: many changes touch 100 or more of the 720 sample towns. So the widest (300 or more towns) have their own entry and every other change is in a family entry that names its items of 100 or more towns; Parts C and E are one line or one entry each as asked. The chair ruled that this cut stands. The short list therefore has more than 40 numbered entries.

**Summary (read this first)**

- Part A (what a page says): 648 items. Part B (checks retired or reshaped): 184. Part C (lists or ceilings grown by ruling): 61. Part D (still wrong, left for later): 452. Part E (the owner's alone): 201. Total: 1546.
- The five widest changes to a page, by sample towns touched (the sample is a fixed set of 720 generated towns):
  - Item 319: The Foundations and Summary line 'Public legitimacy' now prints the Power tab's own label (Legitimacy crisis, Contested, Tolerated, Approved, Endorsed). (720 of 720 sample towns had a legitimacy row that differed from the record; the five labels now print in 278, 149, 135, 90 and 68 towns (the hand-back does not say which count belongs to which label)).
  - Item 214: The two sentences about threat bars now say the table's campaign: 'is re-judged as your campaign goes on'. (720 of 720 sample towns (two sentences, each in all 720)).
  - Item 603: The PDF's Defense & Security caption takes the same new words as the tab ('your campaign goes on'), and the PDF's Overview reads the same constant. The helper calls this its own judgment, because the file was not named as lent. (720 of 720 sample towns).
  - Item 441: In the PDF Overview, the line "Reason settled: <the origin line>" now reads "Settlement Origin: <the origin line>". (720 of 720 sample towns).
  - Item 442: In the Foundry journal's Overview page, the heading "Why this place exists" now reads "Settlement Origin". (720 of 720 sample towns).
- Every change here was made on the understanding that the owner may veto it. Each item says what a veto would do.
- "Count not recorded" means the seat's hand-back gave no town count. Where two hand-backs disagree, both numbers are given.
- Technical handles in square brackets at the end of each item are for the engineer who would carry out a veto.
- The last section is a table that accounts for every line of the hand-backs that mentions a veto or the owner.
- Nothing on this list has been merged or deployed; the merge, the deploy and every database migration remain the owner's.

## The short list: what to decide

This is the top layer. Every entry points to the numbered items of the full list below, where each change is written out with its before and after sentences, its town count and what a veto would do. The widest changes to pages have their own entry; the rest are grouped by kind of change, with the widest items of each kind as examples. "At most" means the same town may be counted under more than one item.

### The widest changes to what pages print (own entry each: 300 or more of the 720 sample towns, widest first; the first entry, if present, is counted on the 525 reference towns instead and is one of the widest changes of the round)

**S1. For the same seed, about half of the reference towns now have a different cast of people: names, personalities, who is tied to whom, and the conflicts between them.**
Towns: 272 of 525 reference towns (not the 720 sample towns).  
If vetoed: The seats of power lose their named holders again and the old casts return for old seeds; every later change built on those people would need measuring again.  
Full list: item 493.

**S2. On the home page, the paragraph under 'advance time' was re-written to tell the story the regenerated sample village now holds: the priest's 'restore order' and the reforms left it; Uathach O'Neill shielding their people and the broken trade routes came in.**
Before: “Then advance time. In Cnocby’s first twelve weeks Étaín Sullivan set out to restore order and the village went onto a war footing; the split between the faiths ended, leaving its sectarian memory behind; by week nine control of the village’s water was passing to the Elder Council; and by week twelve Caoilfhinn Gallagher was pushing through reforms as crime took hold of its streets. Every one of those is a record the engine wrote, and every one carries its cause.” After: “Then advance time. In Cnocby’s first twelve weeks the split between the faiths ended, leaving its sectarian memory behind, and the village went onto a war footing; by week nine control of the village’s water was passing to the Elder Council; then Uathach O'Neill set out to shield their people as crime took hold of its streets; and by week twelve its trade routes had broken down, its traders with little to sell. Every one of those is a record the engine wrote, and every one carries its cause.”  
Towns: the one sample village on the landing page (Cnocby); not a count of towns.  
If vetoed: The old paragraph returns, and its check is then red because the sample no longer holds those events.  
Full list: item 646.

Hook: A family on the brink of ruin blames a rival for stirring the panic, and wants proof. Hook: Someone is quietly buying up other people's debts, and nobody knows who. | 5 |
  | – | [trade collapse] Description: Whether the trade the settlement lives on is about to fail is the quarrel of the day: some see buyers going elsewhere, others see nothing but rumour Parties: Traders who fear the buyers are going elsewhere; Workers afraid for their wages; Rivals who would gain if the trade moved Hook: Someone with power would rather the trade went elsewhere, and is quietly making it harder. Hook: Someone is using the fear of fever to keep a rival household shut indoors, and out of a bargain. | 16 |
  | – | [great flood] Description: Rising water is the settlement's standing fear, and every wet season reopens the quarrel over who must dig the ditches, who keeps the low ground, and who pays for both Parties: Households on the low ground; Landowners on the high ground; Those who say the water will never come Hook: The ditches that carry off the water are choked, and the household bound to clear them refuses.
